item: A Stop on the last Wikidata item batch is named as airplane mode and left pending, not counted as that batch's refusal (R337)
summary: fetch_items read the kill switch only at the top of each batch, so a Stop during the last batch (no next turn to read it) was counted as refused and the run ended done, with a refused tally and no airplane note. A failed batch now reads the switch itself: the run stops, stopped_by_airplane_mode is true, the batch is not counted as refused and stays pending, and no new tally key exists (a Stop is not an outcome, R320). Controls: an earlier ordinary refusal followed by a good last batch is not an airplane stop; an ordinary failure on the last batch is still that batch's refusal. Two of four tests fail on the old code.
